findings.cell_type: cultured human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells
findings.assay: Arraystar Human LncRNA Array v4.0 mRNA probe signal
findings.finding: Table 4 includes a downregulated feature labeled PRAMEF18/PRAMEF19 in treated nonmalignant human vascular-cell cultures.
findings.decision_reason: The combined feature leaves expression of PRAMEF18 in an induced normal-cell state unresolved; hold admission without assigning an Unsafe finding.
findings.source_title: Analysis of lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA Interactions in Hyper-proliferative Human Pulmonary Arterial Smooth Muscle Cells
findings.source_location: Table 4; mRNA array methods; Supplementary File I
findings.limitations: The assay does not separate PRAMEF18 from PRAMEF19. This is a treated nonmalignant culture, not basal healthy lung or protein detection. No exact-copy probe sequence was recovered from Supplementary File I; raw data are available from the authors on request.

findings.review_depth: Primary source and assay-identity review; named-candidate audit 2026-11-08
findings.cell_type: glandular cells; summary highlights endocrine cells
findings.assay: immunohistochemistry; HPA057423
findings.finding: HPA reports medium overall glandular-cell staining with strong intensity in small intestine and duodenum; the antibody reliability is Uncertain and targets more than one gene.
findings.decision_reason: Normal intestinal staining is a review hold until the recognized copy is resolved. Uncertain shared-antibody staining cannot establish PRAMEF18-specific normal protein production.
findings.source_title: Human Protein Atlas: PRAMEF18 tissue expression and antibody validation
findings.source_location: HPA 25 XML retrieved 2026-11-08; antibody HPA057423; tissueExpression normal_tissue and validation summary
findings.limitations: The antibody is not gene-specific. RNA/staining consistency is very low. Neither positive nor negative staining with this reagent establishes exact-copy expression or absence; pinned HPA v23 selection evidence is retained separately.

findings.review_depth: Primary source and assay-identity review; named-candidate audit 2026-11-08
findings.cell_type: producing cell unresolved
findings.state: breast cancer and healthy-control pools combined in the identification table
findings.assay: MALDI-TOF/TOF; MASCOT Swiss-Prot protein identification
findings.finding: Table II lists TRI75_HUMAN (TRIM75) among tear-fluid proteins in a study of 25 breast-cancer patients and 25 healthy women.
findings.decision_reason: Hold normal-restriction clearance until the contributing pool and peptide specificity are resolved. The merged table establishes neither a healthy-control positive nor cancer-specific protein.
findings.source_title: Comparison of tear protein levels in breast cancer patients and healthy controls using a de novo proteomic approach
findings.source_location: Table II; pooled sampling and MALDI identification methods; Table III does not quantify TRIM75
findings.limitations: One pooled tear sample per clinical group. Table II merges identifications and does not assign TRIM75 to a pool or supply its peptide sequences. Tear-fluid detection does not localize the producing tissue or demonstrate a tumor origin.

findings.review_depth: Primary source and assay-identity review; named-candidate audit 2026-11-08
findings.cell_type: reported human eight-cell embryos
findings.state: KDM4A overexpression after tripronuclear zygote correction
findings.assay: reported RT-qPCR; primer identity check
findings.finding: The Ubtfl1 row in Table I cites XM_021185540.2, a Mus caroli Sod1 transcript. Its two primer sequences do not match selected human UBTFL1 ENST00000530464.2 and both match mouse Sod1 ENSMUST00000023707.10.
findings.decision_reason: Do not count this assay as exact-human UBTFL1 support. Independent human embryo RNA and the qualifying coding reference retain their own evidence status.
findings.source_title: Histone demethylase KDM4A overexpression improved the efficiency of corrected human tripronuclear zygote development
findings.source_location: Table I Ubtfl1 primers; Figure 5; NCBI XM_021185540.2 and exact forward/reverse-complement cDNA comparisons
findings.limitations: This finding rejects attribution of this specific assay. It does not reject the other experiments in the paper or establish normal UBTFL1 expression. Mouse Hmgpi and human UBTFL2/3 results cannot be substituted for this copy.

findings.review_depth: Primary source and assay-identity review; named-candidate audit 2026-11-08
findings.cell_type: hepatocellular carcinoma bulk tissue
findings.assay: TCGA RNA-seq differential-expression analysis
findings.finding: Supplementary Table S3 includes TMEM269 as upregulated in TCGA LIHC, log2 fold change 1.257588672, logCPM -3.45323963 and FDR 1.69e-6.
findings.decision_reason: Add exact-symbol tumor RNA context. This paper does not nominate a CTA or demonstrate protein localization, antigen presentation or normal-tissue restriction.
findings.source_title: Identification of potential crucial genes associated with the pathogenesis and prognosis of liver hepatocellular carcinoma
findings.source_location: Supplementary Table S3, PDF page 101; differential-expression table header on page 1
findings.limitations: The supplementary RNA comparison is a reanalysis of TCGA, not an independent tumor cohort. Low average RNA expression and a differential-expression statistic do not establish an accessible membrane protein.

findings.review_depth: Primary source and assay-identity review; named-candidate audit 2026-11-08
findings.cell_type: A2780 ovarian-cancer cell line
findings.assay: RNA sequencing
findings.finding: Table S2 lists SSU72P7, the previous symbol of SSU72L1, with log2 fold change 5.779251523 (54.91968795-fold) and adjusted P 9.14e-69 after CDCA8 knockdown.
findings.decision_reason: Add exact-copy-symbol cancer-cell RNA context, retaining the old symbol. A perturbation response does not establish baseline tumor prevalence, protein production or CTA identity.
findings.source_title: CDCA8, targeted by MYBL2, promotes malignant progression and olaparib insensitivity in ovarian cancer
findings.source_location: Figure 4 and Table S2; combined publisher PDF page 45 (supplement page 18)
findings.limitations: The table reports a gene-level RNA result, not unique-read or peptide validation. SSU72 phosphatase experiments are not transferable to SSU72L1 or to SSU72L2-5.

findings.cell_type: laser-captured human taste-bud compartment
findings.assay: semi-quantitative RT-PCR; TaqMan Hs00699323_m1
findings.finding: Figure 10D reports CALHM3 RNA in laser-captured human circumvallate taste buds relative to surrounding lingual epithelium.
findings.decision_reason: Localized human normal-compartment RNA blocks CTA admission pending protein/cell localization review. The human result cannot be dismissed as mouse-only evidence.

findings.source_location: Figure 10D; human taste-bud results; Methods: qPCR

findings.review_depth: PR 685 primary-source review; all in-scope loci retained
findings.cell_type: unresolved cells in human brain tissue
findings.state: normal whole brain; fetal brain and testis also measured
findings.assay: array-level RT-PCR with no-reverse-transcriptase controls
findings.finding: Figure 4 reports TAF11-like macrosatellite RNA in whole brain, fetal brain and testis. The chromosome 5p15.1 array contains nearly identical coding repeats.
findings.decision_reason: Apply one normal-expression review hold to all represented TAF11-like copies until copy attribution is resolved. Paper coverage does not exempt TAF11L12 or any other copy. Existing Unsafe evidence takes precedence.
findings.source_title: Expression, tandem repeat copy number variation and stability of four macrosatellite arrays in the human genome
findings.source_location: Expression of the TAF11-Like array; Figure 4; Table 1; Ensembl 115 reference scope saved in taf11-like-scope.csv
findings.limitations: The shared assay identifies neither the expressing modern copy nor protein production. The 13 reference coding loci are review scope, not 13 positives. Family-level cancer/testis nomination cannot remove the normal-brain finding.
